subject: Python Setup
title: Run Your First Python File | Day 1
outcome: install Python, use the interactive shell, and run a saved Python file
demo: Run hello.py, then change its greeting and run it again. Compare 10 + 20 in the shell with print(10 + 20) in a file.
trap: Typing a terminal command at the >>> Python prompt
question: Why does your Python file show nothing when the shell shows 30?
challenge: Print your name, calculate 10 + 20, and inspect type(30), type(3.5), and type('Python').
beats: Show the working greeting before explaining installation
Verify Python 3 and distinguish the terminal from the Python shell
Use arithmetic, quoted text, print(), and one deliberate syntax error
Save hello.py in VS Code, run it from the correct folder, and preview the Day 1 type examples
short: A shell expression and a saved script do not display results the same way

subject: Python Variables
title: Python Variables and input() | Day 2
outcome: store user input and convert text into numbers
demo: Ask for a learner's name and age. Print the name and calculate next year's age after int() conversion.
trap: Assuming input() returns a number
question: Why does your Python input fail when you add 1?
challenge: Collect two numbers, print their sum, and display their types before and after conversion.
beats: Show an age calculation failing, then the corrected output
Name variables clearly and inspect values with type()
Demonstrate input(), int(), float(), str(), and len()
Use help(), dir(), min(), max(), and sum() as a reference tour rather than a memorization test
short: input() returns text even when you type digits

subject: Python Operators
title: Python Operators: / vs // | Day 3
outcome: choose arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators deliberately
demo: Divide 17 items into groups of 5. Compare /, //, and %, then evaluate whether a price is inside a range.
trap: Treating == and is as interchangeable
question: What happens when you split 17 items into groups of 5 in Python?
challenge: Calculate quotient and remainder, then test whether a sample age is within a chosen range.
beats: Show three outputs from the same two numbers
Explain assignment, arithmetic, and augmented assignment
Predict comparison and and/or/not results before running
Contrast equality, identity, and membership with separate examples
short: 17 divided by 5 has three useful answers in Python

subject: Python Strings
title: Python Strings: Clean Text | Day 4
outcome: clean and format text using string methods and slicing
demo: Turn '  aNa  ' into 'Ana', split a comma-separated label, and build a greeting with an f-string.
trap: Expecting a string method to change the original variable automatically
question: Why does your Python string stay messy after you call strip()?
challenge: Normalize a padded name, extract its first three characters, and print a formatted greeting.
beats: Show raw and cleaned text side by side
Create strings and explain escapes and indexes
Use slicing, strip(), replace(), split(), and join()
Compare f-strings with older formatting syntax; use the method table as the lab reference
short: strip() returns a new string; it does not rewrite the old one

subject: Python Lists
title: Python Lists: sort() vs sorted() | Day 5
outcome: edit a list and distinguish in-place changes from returned values
demo: Create a course-topic list, append an item, remove one, then compare sort() with sorted().
trap: Assigning the return value of list.sort() back to the list
question: Why does your Python list become None after sorting?
challenge: Copy a list of scores, sort the copy, and prove the original order survived.
beats: Show the None result and keep the fix open
Build, index, slice, and update a list
Compare append(), extend(), remove(), and pop()
Demonstrate copy(), sort(), and sorted() with original and result visible
short: sort() changes the list and returns None

subject: Python Tuples
title: Python Tuples: The Comma Rule | Day 6
outcome: create tuples and unpack fixed collections
demo: Compare type((5)) and type((5,)); unpack a coordinate pair into x and y.
trap: Assuming parentheses alone create a one-item tuple
question: Why is your one-item Python tuple still an integer?
challenge: Create a three-item tuple, unpack it, and rebuild it with one changed value.
beats: Reveal the two types from nearly identical expressions
Create empty, single-item, and multi-item tuples
Index, slice, count, search, and unpack
Demonstrate why item reassignment fails and when a list is a better fit
short: The comma makes a one-item tuple

subject: Python Sets
title: Python Sets: Remove Duplicates | Day 7
outcome: deduplicate values and compare membership across groups
demo: Compare registered learners and attendees using intersection and difference; show repeated names collapsing in a set.
trap: Expecting sets to preserve list positions or support indexing
question: What happens to your list order when Python removes duplicates with a set?
challenge: Find learners who registered but did not attend, then find everyone in either group.
beats: Show duplicate names collapsing and explain the order tradeoff
Create sets correctly, including set() for an empty set
Add and remove values; compare remove() with discard()
Visualize union, intersection, difference, and symmetric difference using the mind map
short: An empty pair of braces is a dictionary, not a set

subject: Python Dictionaries
title: Python Dictionaries: get() | Day 8
outcome: store a learner record and handle a missing dictionary key
demo: Build a name-and-score dictionary; request an absent email with square brackets and with get().
trap: Confusing key membership with value membership
question: Why does your Python dictionary fail when one field is missing?
challenge: Add a learner field, update a score, and read an optional field with a default.
beats: Show a missing field and the two retrieval behaviors
Create and update key-value pairs
Read keys(), values(), and items(); explain membership
Copy, remove, and clear entries while keeping the original record visible
short: get() lets you choose a default for a missing key

subject: Python Conditionals
title: Python if, elif, else | Day 9
outcome: write decisions with mutually exclusive branches
demo: Classify a sample score into a grade using descending thresholds, then compare with separate if statements.
trap: Putting a broad condition before a more specific one
question: Why does your Python grade checker choose the wrong branch?
challenge: Write a score classifier and test values exactly on either side of each boundary.
beats: Show a boundary value taking an unexpected branch
Explain indentation and if/else
Order elif conditions and contrast independent if statements
Combine conditions with and/or and simplify unnecessary nesting
short: The first true elif branch wins

subject: Python Loops
title: Python Loops: range() | Day 10
outcome: repeat work with for and while and control loop flow
demo: Print labels for days 1 through 5, then skip one day with continue and stop early with break.
trap: Forgetting that range() excludes the stop value
question: Why does your Python loop stop before day 5?
challenge: Sum a range of numbers and write a while loop whose condition eventually becomes false.
beats: Show range(1, 5) and ask which number is missing
Iterate lists, strings, dictionaries, tuples, and sets
Explain while, updates, break, and continue
Trace a small nested loop and distinguish loop else from if else
short: range(1, 5) stops at 4

subject: Python Functions
title: Python Functions: return vs print | Day 11
outcome: build a reusable function that returns a result
demo: Refactor a score calculation into a function and show why printing inside it does not supply a reusable return value.
trap: Confusing what a function prints with what it returns
question: Why does your Python function print an answer but return None?
challenge: Write a total function with a default argument, call it twice, and use its returned value in another calculation.
beats: Print a result and separately inspect the returned value
Define, call, and parameterize a function
Use return, defaults, and keyword arguments
Introduce *args, **kwargs, unpacking, and functions as arguments with small examples
short: A printed answer is not a returned answer

subject: Python Modules
title: Python Modules: Import Your Code | Day 12
outcome: reuse a function from another Python file
demo: Move a helper into helpers.py and import it from main.py; compare a local module with math and statistics.
trap: Naming a local file random.py and shadowing the standard library
question: Why does your Python import load the wrong file?
challenge: Create a helpers module and use math.sqrt() and statistics.mean() from a separate script.
beats: Show one function reused from another file
Create a module and use import and from imports
Use aliases and inspect where an import came from
Tour os, sys, statistics, math, string, and random with one focused example each
short: Your filename can hide a Python standard-library module

subject: Python List Comprehensions
title: Python List Comprehensions | Day 13
outcome: translate a readable loop into a filtered list comprehension
demo: Build squares of even numbers first with append(), then with a comprehension, and compare results.
trap: Compressing a complicated nested transformation until it is unreadable
question: How can you turn a Python loop into one list expression?
challenge: Filter positive numbers and transform them; write the equivalent loop beside the comprehension.
beats: Reveal identical outputs from loop and comprehension
Map expression, iteration, and filter positions
Flatten a small two-dimensional list in the correct loop order
Introduce lambda separately and explain when a named function is clearer
short: Read a comprehension as output, loop, then filter

subject: Python Higher Order Functions
title: Python Decorators Explained | Day 14
outcome: understand functions as values and build a small decorator
demo: Pass a formatter into another function, then wrap a greeting with before-and-after messages.
trap: Calling a function when you meant to pass the function itself
question: What changes when you pass a Python function without parentheses?
challenge: Write a wrapper that accepts arguments and preserves the wrapped function's return value.
beats: Show a function traveling as an argument
Explain returned functions and a closure with one captured value
Build and apply a decorator, including argument forwarding
Compare map(), filter(), reduce(), and sorted(key=...) without presenting them as mandatory replacements for loops
short: greet and greet() are different things

subject: Python Errors
title: Read Python Tracebacks | Day 15
outcome: read an error message and locate the failing expression
demo: Trigger a NameError, an IndexError, and a TypeError, then fix the relevant line in each case.
trap: Changing unrelated code before reading the exception type and final traceback frame
question: Where should you look first when Python shows a traceback?
challenge: Repair three broken snippets and explain each error in one sentence.
beats: Freeze one traceback and identify its useful parts
Fix syntax, name, index, and key errors
Separate attribute, import, and missing-module failures
Contrast TypeError, ValueError, and ZeroDivisionError using the course examples
short: Read the exception message, then the final traceback frame

subject: Python datetime
title: Python datetime: Parse Dates | Day 16
outcome: parse, format, and subtract dates
demo: Parse '2026-10-08' with strptime(), format it for display, and calculate the interval to another fixed date.
trap: Confusing the input format with the desired display format
question: Why does your Python date parse fail even when the date looks right?
challenge: Parse two known dates and report their difference in days, including a month boundary.
beats: Show a date string becoming a datetime object
Inspect year, month, day, and time components
Contrast strptime() with strftime() and use the format-code reference
Subtract dates and add timedelta without manually counting month lengths
short: strptime parses; strftime formats

subject: Python Exceptions
title: Python try and except | Day 17
outcome: handle an expected conversion error without hiding unrelated failures
demo: Convert sample input to an integer and catch ValueError; demonstrate else and finally with visible messages.
trap: Using a broad exception handler that conceals a programming bug
question: How can you stop one bad Python input from ending your program?
challenge: Handle a bad numeric input with a useful message, then pair labels and values using zip().
beats: Show a failed conversion and a specific recovery path
Explain try, except, else, and finally
Compare specific exceptions with a broad Exception handler
Connect packing, unpacking, enumerate(), and zip() to readable input processing
short: Catch the error you expect, not every possible failure

subject: Python Regex
title: Python Regex: Find Patterns | Day 18
outcome: extract and replace simple text patterns with re
demo: Extract sample order numbers from a short log and replace repeated whitespace with a single space.
trap: Using match() when the desired pattern begins later in the text
question: Why does your Python regex miss a pattern that is clearly there?
challenge: Find all numeric order IDs and explain the difference between search(), match(), and findall().
beats: Highlight desired matches before showing the pattern
Introduce raw strings and the re module
Compare match(), search(), findall(), sub(), and split()
Build character classes and quantifiers before previewing groups, flags, and lookaheads
short: match() starts at the beginning; search() looks through the string

subject: Python Files
title: Python Files: Save Your Data | Day 19
outcome: save and reload learner data using text, JSON, and CSV
demo: Write a learner record to JSON, close the program, and load the record in a new run.
trap: Opening an existing file with w when you intended to append
question: Why does your Python file lose its old contents when you save again?
challenge: Save a dictionary as JSON and reload it; append a log entry without overwriting previous entries.
beats: Restart the script and show saved data surviving
Use with open(), explicit encoding, and read methods
Contrast write and append with a disposable example file
Serialize JSON, read CSV, and position XLSX/XML as separate file formats with their own tools
short: w replaces file contents; a appends

subject: Python pip
title: Python pip: Install Packages | Day 20
outcome: install and inspect a package in the intended Python environment
demo: Open with a pre-recorded result from a prepared environment, labeled FINISHED DEMO. For the learner code-along, create and select the project environment, run python -m pip install requests, then inspect python -m pip --version and python -m pip show requests before making the HTTP request. Package downloads and the live request need an internet connection.
trap: Installing into a different interpreter from the one that runs the script
question: Why does your Python import fail after pip says the package is installed?
challenge: Install a package in a project environment, inspect its version, and save its dependency list.
beats: Show the labeled finished demo, then connect package location to the selected interpreter
Preview Day 23 with python -m venv and select that environment before installing dependencies
Install requests before the import example, then show, list, freeze, and uninstall using python -m pip
Read a URL after installation, explain the network requirement, and inspect a minimal local package structure
short: python -m pip ties pip to the interpreter you selected

subject: Python Classes
title: Python Classes and Objects | Day 21
outcome: model learners as objects with separate instance state
demo: Create two Student objects, update one score with a method, and show that the other score stays unchanged.
trap: Accidentally sharing mutable class-level state between instances
question: Why did changing one Python object affect another object?
challenge: Create two instances with independent fields and override one method in a subclass.
beats: Show two objects with distinct values
Define a class, __init__(), and instance attributes
Write methods and distinguish instance from class attributes
Demonstrate inheritance and method overriding with one small extension
short: Put per-object mutable data on self inside __init__

subject: Python Web Scraping
title: Python Web Scraping | Day 22
outcome: extract structured records from HTML with Beautiful Soup
demo: Parse a small saved HTML table first, then fetch a public example page and export selected rows as JSON.
trap: Assuming the HTML response contains everything a JavaScript-driven browser displays
question: Why can you see a table in your browser but not in Python's HTML response?
challenge: Extract headings and table rows from a known HTML sample and save a structured JSON file.
beats: Show the raw HTML beside the extracted table
Fetch and inspect status, text, and content
Use find(), find_all(), select(), and attributes on a saved sample
Export records and compare server HTML with browser-rendered content
short: The server response and the rendered page can differ

subject: Python Virtual Environments
title: Python venv: Isolate Packages | Day 23
outcome: create, activate, inspect, and recreate a project environment
demo: Create two environments and install Flask in only one; compare the interpreter and installed-package lists.
trap: Assuming the editor selected the interpreter from the activated terminal
question: Why does your Python editor miss a package that works in your terminal?
challenge: Create .venv, install Flask, save requirements.txt, and identify the selected interpreter.
beats: Show different package lists in two environments
Create an environment with python -m venv .venv
Show platform-specific activation and select the editor interpreter
Freeze dependencies, deactivate, and explain why .venv is excluded from source control
short: Activation and the editor's interpreter selection are separate checks

subject: Python Statistics
title: Python Statistics and NumPy | Day 24
outcome: compare summary statistics and use NumPy arrays for calculations
demo: Calculate mean and median for [10, 10, 10, 10, 100], then perform an elementwise calculation on a NumPy array.
trap: Treating a mean as a complete description of a skewed dataset
question: Which average describes your Python data when one value is much larger?
challenge: Compare mean, median, sample standard deviation, and population standard deviation on an explicit dataset.
beats: Show one large value moving the mean away from the median
Use the statistics module and distinguish sample from population measures
Create arrays and inspect shape, dtype, and slicing
Demonstrate elementwise operations, reshaping, and the course's NumPy reference examples
short: Mean and median answer different questions about the same data

subject: Python pandas
title: Python pandas: Read a CSV | Day 25
outcome: load, inspect, filter, and update a small DataFrame
demo: Use a CSV with columns name,score and rows Ana,85 and Ben,60. Deliberately read it with pd.read_csv('learners.csv', dtype={'score': str}) to demonstrate text import. Show that df['score'] > 70 raises TypeError, then convert with df['score'] = pd.to_numeric(df['score']) and filter again to return Ana. Explain that an ordinary read_csv often infers this numeric column correctly.
trap: Comparing numeric-looking strings as though the column were numeric
question: Why does your Python pandas filter fail on a column full of numbers?
challenge: Read a CSV with score explicitly imported as text, convert it to numbers, and add a calculated column.
beats: Show the exact row the finished filter should return and label the deliberate text-import setup
Introduce Series and DataFrames with the two-row name-and-score table
Use read_csv() with dtype={'score': str}, then head(), shape, info(), and describe()
Reproduce the text-versus-number TypeError, convert with pd.to_numeric(), add a column, and repeat the Boolean filter
short: Check your column dtype before trusting a numeric filter

subject: Python Flask
title: Python Flask: Build a Web Page | Day 26
outcome: serve a page and process a simple form with Flask
demo: Run a local Flask site with home and about routes, then submit text to a form and display a result.
trap: Treating a development server as the final deployment setup
question: How does your Python function become a page in a browser?
challenge: Create a shared layout, add navigation, and make a POST form return a result.
beats: Show the local page and the form result
Create the project environment and route functions
Add templates, layout inheritance, navigation, and static files
Trace GET versus POST; treat the source's Heroku screens as historical deployment material pending revalidation
short: A route connects a browser request to a Python function

subject: Python MongoDB
title: Python MongoDB: Store Records | Day 27
outcome: insert, query, update, and delete sample MongoDB documents
demo: Insert a sample student document, find it by a field, update its score, and show the changed record.
trap: Looking up an ObjectId using an unconverted string
question: Why can your Python MongoDB query miss a document whose ID you copied?
challenge: Insert sample records, query scores with $gt, project selected fields, and update one record.
beats: Show a document surviving an app restart
Explain collections, documents, fields, and _id
Connect with PyMongo and demonstrate insert/find/projection/sort/limit
Update and delete a sample document; explain ObjectId conversion before the API lesson
short: A string ID and an ObjectId are different values

subject: Python APIs
title: Python APIs: HTTP Explained | Day 28
outcome: read an HTTP request and response before building an API
demo: Inspect one request's method and URL, then its response status, headers, and JSON body in browser tools or Postman.
trap: Assuming every response body is valid JSON
question: What does your Python app receive when an API sends an error page?
challenge: Inspect a JSON response and an error response; record status code, Content-Type, and body separately.
beats: Show the request and response side by side
Explain URL, method, headers, and optional body
Read status and Content-Type before interpreting a response
Map GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE to the students API planned for Day 29
short: A 200 status and a JSON body are separate facts to inspect

subject: Python REST API
title: Build a Python REST API | Day 29
outcome: build and exercise a small Flask students API with CRUD routes
demo: Create a sample student with POST, read it with GET, update with PUT, and delete it while inspecting each response.
trap: Returning a success-shaped response for a missing record
question: What should your Python API return when a student ID does not exist?
challenge: Implement a missing-record 404 and confirm it in Postman alongside the successful CRUD path.
beats: Show the completed request-response sequence
Start with GET and dummy JSON before adding the database
Add POST, PUT, and DELETE with explicit input and ID handling
Test valid, invalid, and missing records; connect status codes back to Day 28
short: Missing data should produce an intentional response, not an accidental crash

subject: Python Projects
title: After 30 Days of Python: Build This
outcome: choose a small next project and define what finished means
demo: Open the working students API, a CSV analysis, and a log-summary sketch, then choose one path using a concrete acceptance checklist.
trap: Starting another full course without finishing an independent project
question: What can you build with Python when the tutorial is closed?
challenge: Finish one unfinished exercise and write a ten-line next-project plan with a clear definition of done.
beats: Run a previous project without following the lesson
Recall environments, HTTP methods, database terms, and a fundamentals script
Choose web, data, or automation using the course's suggested project paths
Set a one-week project scope and demonstrate how to check completion
short: Define done before choosing your next Python project
